questions.questionText: What does MD&A stand for in annual reports?
questions.hint: It's found in annual reports explaining company performance
questions.explanation: MD&A stands for Management Discussion and Analysis, which provides context for financial performance

questions.questionText: What type of account is unearned revenue?
questions.hint: This represents money received for services not yet provided
questions.explanation: Unearned revenue is a liability because the company owes services to customers

questions.questionText: Which of the following best describes an accrued expense?

options.text: Expense incurred but not yet paid
Expense paid but not yet incurred

questions.hint: It relates to the timing of recognition
questions.explanation: Accrued expenses are costs incurred during a period but not yet paid

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of the general ledger?
questions.hint: It's the main accounting record
questions.explanation: The general ledger contains all financial transactions of the business

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a TRANSACTION, not an ADJUSTMENT?
questions.hint: This involves actual cash movement
questions.explanation: Recording cash received is a transaction, while depreciation and accruals are adjustments

questions.questionText: Which of the following lists the steps of the accounting cycle in the correct order?

options.text: Journal, Ledger, Trial Balance, Financial Statements
Ledger, Journal, Trial Balance, Financial Statements
Trial Balance, Journal, Ledger, Financial Statements
Financial Statements, Trial Balance, Ledger, Journal

questions.hint: Start with recording, then classify, then summarize
questions.explanation: The correct order is: Journalize transactions, post to ledger, prepare trial balance, prepare financial statements

questions.questionText: What is the best type of auditor's report a company can earn?
questions.hint: This opinion states financial statements are fairly presented
questions.explanation: An unqualified opinion means the financial statements are free from material misstatements

questions.questionText: Which of the following lists the sections of an annual report from MOST GENERAL to MOST SPECIFIC?
questions.hint: Start with the big picture, then details
questions.explanation: Annual reports go from general overview to specific notes

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an adjustment for an accrued revenue?

options.text: Debit Accounts Receivable, Credit Service Revenue
Debit Service Revenue, Credit Accounts Receivable

questions.hint: Revenue earned but not yet received
questions.explanation: Accrued revenue requires recognizing revenue and an asset

questions.questionText: When does ACCRUAL accounting record revenues and expenses?

options.text: When cash is received or paid
At the end of the year

questions.hint: It's about timing of recognition, not cash flow
questions.explanation: Accrual accounting records revenues when earned and expenses when incurred

questions.questionText: In the absence of a Partnership Deed, the rate of interest on a partner's loan to the firm is:
questions.hint: It's set by the Indian Partnership Act
questions.explanation: Under the Indian Partnership Act, in the absence of a deed, interest is allowed at 6% p.a.

questions.questionText: Goodwill is a/an:
questions.hint: It can't be physically touched or seen
questions.explanation: Goodwill is an intangible/fictitious asset that represents reputation

questions.questionText: On the admission of a new partner, the balance of General Reserve in the Balance Sheet is transferred to:
questions.hint: It belongs to existing partners
questions.explanation: General Reserve is distributed among old partners before admission

questions.questionText: Revaluation Account is a:
questions.hint: It follows the principle of debit what comes in
questions.explanation: Revaluation Account is a Real Account used to revalue assets

questions.questionText: The maximum number of partners allowed in a firm as per the Companies Act, 2013 is:
questions.hint: There's a specific number mentioned in the Act
questions.explanation: The Companies Act 2013 limits partnerships to 50 members

questions.questionText: Interest on a partner's drawing is charged at:
questions.hint: It's calculated on the amount withdrawn
questions.explanation: Interest on drawings is charged at simple interest rate

questions.questionText: Securities Premium Reserve can be used for:

options.text: Issue of fully paid-up bonus shares

questions.hint: It can be utilized for specific purposes under the Act
questions.explanation: Securities Premium can be used for issuing bonus shares under Section 78

questions.questionText: When shares are forfeited, the Share Forfeiture Account is credited with:
questions.hint: It's the difference between called-up and received
questions.explanation: Share Forfeiture Account is credited with the amount called-up but not received

questions.questionText: Analysis of Financial Statements is a tool for:
questions.hint: It helps evaluate performance
questions.explanation: Financial statement analysis assesses the financial health of a business

questions.questionText: Calls in Arrears are:
questions.hint: It represents unpaid calls
questions.explanation: Calls in Arrears represent called-up capital not yet paid by shareholders

questions.questionText: What are liabilities?
questions.hint: It's what the business owes
questions.explanation: Liabilities are amounts owed to others (creditors)

questions.questionText: A credit to the accounts receivable account indicates:

options.text: A sale to customers on account has occurred
A payment from customers on their account has been received

questions.hint: Think about what decreases accounts receivable
questions.explanation: Credit to AR indicates payment received, reducing the amount owed

questions.questionText: A debit is the normal balance for which account?
questions.hint: Asset accounts have debit balances
questions.explanation: Accounts Receivable is an asset with a debit balance

questions.questionText: What is revenue?
questions.hint: It's income from business activities
questions.explanation: Revenue is income from sales of goods or services

questions.questionText: What are expenses?

options.text: Cost of selling products or services

questions.hint: They reduce profit
questions.explanation: Expenses are costs incurred to generate revenue

questions.questionText: Owner's equity is:
questions.hint: Use the accounting equation
questions.explanation: Owner's equity = Assets - Liabilities

questions.questionText: A business paid its supplier $1,000 to satisfy an accounts payable balance. How should this be recorded?

options.text: Debit accounts payable and credit cash for $1,000
Debit cash and credit accounts payable for $1,000
Debit supplies expense and credit cash for $1,000
Debit accounts receivable and credit cash for $1,000

questions.hint: Both asset and liability decrease
questions.explanation: Paying AP decreases both cash and accounts payable

questions.questionText: A business borrowed $1,000 from the bank and debited its cash account. What else is needed?
questions.hint: There's a new liability created
questions.explanation: Borrowing creates a liability (Notes Payable) that must be credited

questions.questionText: During a period, total assets increase by $500 and total liabilities decrease by $200. By how much does owner's equity change?
questions.hint: Use A = L + OE
questions.explanation: ΔAssets = ΔLiabilities + ΔOE, so 500 = -200 + ΔOE, therefore ΔOE = 700

questions.questionText: What is the accounting equation?
questions.hint: The basic foundation of accounting
questions.explanation: Assets = Liabilities + Owner's Equity is the fundamental accounting equation

questions.questionText: Which node in the provided accounting cycle flow represents the first formal record of a transaction?
questions.hint: It's the book of original entry
questions.explanation: The Journal is the first place transactions are recorded in chronological order.

questions.questionText: What are outstanding checks in a bank reconciliation?

options.text: Checks written but not yet cleared by bank
Checks received but not yet deposited

questions.hint: Think about timing differences
questions.explanation: Outstanding checks are those issued by the company but not yet presented to the bank for payment.

questions.questionText: Which depreciation method results in higher expense in the early years of an asset's life?
questions.hint: It's an accelerated method
questions.explanation: Accelerated methods like double-declining balance allocate more cost to early years.

questions.questionText: In a period of rising prices, which inventory method results in the highest Net Income?
questions.hint: FIFO uses older, cheaper costs for COGS
questions.explanation: FIFO assigns older (lower) costs to COGS, resulting in higher gross profit and net income when prices rise.

questions.questionText: Which ratio measures a company's ability to pay short-term obligations with its most liquid assets?
questions.hint: Also known as the Acid-Test Ratio
questions.explanation: The Quick Ratio excludes inventory from current assets to measure immediate liquidity.

questions.questionText: Based on the T-account flow, where is the final balance of the Cash account typically transferred?
questions.hint: It summarizes all account balances
questions.explanation: Balances from ledger accounts (T-accounts) are collected into the Trial Balance.

questions.questionText: If the Trial Balance debits and credits are equal, does it guarantee no errors were made?

options.text: No, some errors do not affect equality
Yes, it is the ultimate proof of accuracy
Yes, provided the math is correct
No, it only checks asset accounts

questions.hint: Think about double errors or omitted entries
questions.explanation: Errors like omitting a transaction or posting to the wrong account still maintain debit/credit equality.

questions.questionText: Which financial statement reports the financial position of a company at a specific point in time?
questions.hint: It's like a financial snapshot
questions.explanation: The Balance Sheet provides a snapshot of assets, liabilities, and equity at a specific date.

questions.questionText: According to the revenue recognition principle, when should revenue be recorded?

options.text: When it is earned, regardless of cash timing
When cash is received from the customer
At the end of the fiscal year

questions.hint: Core principle of accrual accounting
questions.explanation: Revenue is recognized when the performance obligation is satisfied (earned).

questions.questionText: In the provided internal control flow, which step represents 'Segregation of Duties'?
questions.hint: Dividing responsibilities to prevent fraud
questions.explanation: Segregation of duties ensures that different individuals are responsible for related activities, like recording and custody.

questions.questionText: Under which section of the Cash Flow Statement would 'Dividends Paid' typically be classified in a Grade 12 NSC context?
questions.hint: It relates to the cost of capital from shareholders
questions.explanation: In South African Accounting standards (IFRS for SMEs), dividends paid are classified under Financing Activities.

questions.questionText: A company has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.8:1. If they take out a large long-term loan, how will this ratio likely change?
questions.hint: More debt means a higher numerator in the ratio
questions.explanation: The debt-equity ratio (Long-term debt : Shareholders' Equity) increases when additional debt is incurred.

questions.questionText: Which inventory system requires a physical stock count to determine the Cost of Sales at the end of the year?
questions.hint: Cost of sales is not calculated at the time of each sale
questions.explanation: The periodic system calculates cost of sales at year-end using: Opening Stock + Purchases - Closing Stock.

questions.questionText: VAT on goods purchased by a business for resale is known as:
questions.hint: The business can 'claim back' this VAT from SARS
questions.explanation: Input VAT is the tax paid by a vendor on purchases and is deductible from Output VAT.

questions.questionText: What is the primary purpose of preparing a Bank Reconciliation Statement?

options.text: To identify discrepancies between the Cash Book and Bank Statement
To pay the monthly bank charges
To record depreciation on bank equipment

questions.hint: It ensures the bank balance is accurate
questions.explanation: Bank reconciliation identifies timing differences and errors between internal and external records.

questions.questionText: In the provided flow of asset disposal, what does the final 'Result' node represent if the sale price is LESS than the book value?
questions.hint: Book Value = Cost - Accum Depr
questions.explanation: A loss is incurred when the selling price (proceeds) is lower than the carrying amount (book value).

questions.questionText: Based on the Manufacturing Cost components diagram, which node represents the sum of Direct Materials and Direct Labor?
questions.hint: Prime costs are direct costs of production
questions.explanation: Prime Cost = Direct Materials + Direct Labor. Adding Factory Overheads gives Total Manufacturing Cost.

questions.questionText: If the 'Provision for Bad Debts' needs to be INCREASED, what is the effect on the Income Statement?

options.text: It is recorded as Other Income
It is recorded as an Operating Expense
It has no effect on profit
It is added directly to Retained Income

questions.hint: Increasing a provision reflects a potential loss
questions.explanation: An increase in Provision for Bad Debts is treated as an expense (adjustment), reducing net profit.

questions.questionText: Which ratio is the most important for shareholders to evaluate their return compared to other investment opportunities?
questions.hint: It measures profit earned per Rand of equity invested
questions.explanation: Return on Shareholders' Equity (ROE) shows how effectively management is using shareholders' capital.

questions.questionText: A business has 100 units at R10 and 200 units at R13. Using the Weighted Average method, what is the value per unit?
questions.hint: Total Cost / Total Units

questions.questionText: In the VAT Flow diagram, what happens when 'Output VAT' (tax on sales) is GREATER than 'Input VAT' (tax on purchases)?

options.text: The business gets a refund from SARS
The business owes money to SARS
SARS pays interest to the business

questions.hint: The business is a tax collector for the government
questions.explanation: VAT Payable = Output VAT - Input VAT. If Output > Input, the difference must be paid to SARS.

questions.questionText: According to the Bank Rec Flow diagram, which of these items would be an 'Adjustment' to the Cash Book?
questions.hint: Adjustments are for items known by the bank but not yet in the company books
questions.explanation: Bank charges, interest, and debit orders are added to the Cash Book during the reconciliation process.

questions.questionText: What is the first step in recording the disposal of an asset during the middle of a financial year?

options.text: Calculating depreciation for the current period

questions.hint: You must bring the book value up to date
questions.explanation: Depreciation must be calculated and recorded from the start of the year until the date of disposal.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is classified as a Factory Overhead?

options.text: Sales commission for the marketing team

questions.hint: Indirect production costs in the factory
questions.explanation: Factory cleaners' wages are indirect labor and form part of Factory Overheads.

questions.questionText: In the Shareholders' Equity structure diagram, what represents the earnings kept by the company for future growth?
questions.hint: It's the accumulated profit not paid out as dividends
questions.explanation: Retained Income is the component of equity that consists of accumulated profits reinvested in the business.

questions.questionText: A high stock turnover rate generally indicates:

options.text: Too much capital tied up in stock

questions.hint: It measures how quickly stock is sold
questions.explanation: A high turnover rate suggests that stock is being sold quickly, which is good for liquidity and reducing storage costs.

questions.questionText: In a period of inflation, using FIFO will result in:
questions.hint: Latest purchases remain in stock
questions.explanation: FIFO assumes the first items in are sold first, so the closing stock consists of the most recent (more expensive) purchases.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of an EXEMPT item for VAT purposes in South Africa?
questions.hint: Different from zero-rated; no VAT is charged at all
questions.explanation: Educational services, interest, and residential rent are exempt from VAT, meaning no VAT is charged and no input VAT can be claimed.

questions.questionText: An R800 check received from a debtor was returned by the bank marked 'R/D' (Refer to Drawer). How is this recorded?

options.text: Credit Cash Book and Debit Bank Statement
Debit Debtors Control and Credit Bank (Cash Book)
Debit Bank and Credit Debtors Control

questions.hint: The debtor now owes the money again
questions.explanation: An R/D check must be cancelled by crediting the bank (reducing cash) and re-debiting the debtor's account.

questions.questionText: In the T-Account relationship diagram for disposal, which account is used to consolidate all values to calculate Profit or Loss?
questions.hint: It acts as a temporary clearing account
questions.explanation: The Asset Disposal account is where the cost, accumulated depreciation, and sale price are matched to find the net result.

questions.questionText: Total Manufacturing Cost is R500,000. Opening Work in Progress is R50,000 and Closing Work in Progress is R30,000. What is the Cost of Finished Goods Produced?
questions.hint: Cost of Production = Total Manuf. Cost + Opening WIP - Closing WIP

questions.questionText: Where would 'Proceeds from issue of shares' appear on the Cash Flow Statement?
questions.hint: It involves changes in share capital
questions.explanation: Issuing shares is a way to raise capital, which is a financing activity.

questions.questionText: Based on the Liquidity Components diagram, what is the key difference between the Current Ratio and the Acid-Test Ratio?

options.text: The Acid-Test ratio includes bank overdrafts

questions.hint: Stock is the least liquid current asset
questions.explanation: The Acid-Test ratio (Liquid Ratio) measures immediate liquidity by excluding inventory from current assets.

questions.questionText: According to the Prudence Concept, inventory should be valued at:

options.text: Lower of cost or net realisable value
Higher of cost or net realisable value

questions.hint: Don't overstate assets
questions.explanation: If the market value (NRV) falls below the cost, the stock must be written down to prevent overstating assets.

questions.questionText: When an owner takes goods for personal use, how should VAT be handled?

options.text: Output VAT is charged on the cost price

questions.hint: The business is 'selling' to the owner
questions.explanation: Drawings of stock are deemed supplies; the business must account for Output VAT on the cost of the items taken.

questions.questionText: Based on the Check Status Flow, when does an issued check become 'Stale' in South Africa?
questions.hint: Banks will usually not honor these checks
questions.explanation: A check older than 6 months is stale and must be cancelled in the Cash Book (debited).

questions.questionText: In a trade-in transaction, the 'trade-in value' allowed by the supplier acts as:

options.text: The cost of the new asset
The selling price of the old asset

questions.hint: It's the proceeds received for the old asset
questions.explanation: The trade-in allowance is the effective sale price of the old asset, reducing the amount owed for the new one.

questions.questionText: According to the Labor Cost Flow diagram, what is the cost of 'Direct Labor' to the factory?
questions.hint: Consider the total expense to the business
questions.explanation: The cost to the employer is the Gross Wage plus any additional contributions like UIF or pension fund contributions.

questions.questionText: Based on the Retained Income flow, what happens when Dividends Declared exceed the Net Profit for the year?
questions.hint: Dividends are paid out of profits
questions.explanation: If more is paid out than earned, the company is using up its accumulated reserves from previous years.

questions.questionText: The Dividend Yield is 8% and the market price per share is R12.50. What is the dividend per share?
questions.hint: Dividend Yield = (DPS / Market Price) * 100
